units.la: Qui in peregrinas regiones amandantur, si occasio ita ferat commodaad parentes & patronos aliquid fructuum novorum aut aliarum rerum insignium obviarum mittere solent. Vestro beneficio ego cum aliis quibusdam popularibus in hanc schola confirmandi imprimis studii theologici gratia ablegatus fui. Ut hinc aliud aliquid, quam quod ad studia pertineat ad vos destinem non finit mea erga vos observantia: ut nempe intelligatis, id mihi & caeteris curae esse, quod vestra auctoritate jussistis. Quum vero noveritis, patres multum colendi, exercitatione multa opus esse, ut etiam mediocritatem aliquam in optimis literis aslequamur: non debui praeceptoribus refragari qui me etiam in publicum prodire nunc volebant. Suscepi igitur hanc de amplitudine ecclesiae disputationem, quam advos mittendam duxi, tum ut videatis, quænam sint illa studia in quibus doctores nostri nos hic assidue exercent, tum, ut quo nunc possem modo gratum animum debita cum reverentia erga vestrā dignitatem contestarer. Accipite igitur, viri clarissimi patres plurimum colendi, hoc qualecunque mei studii & in vos affectūs testimonium deincépsq; favorem erga me & reliquos alumnos pietatis vestræ conservate. Deo nos bene juvante, operam daturi sumus necconcepta de nobis exspectatio vos fallat.
units.tr: Those who are sent away to foreign regions are accustomed, if the opportunity allows, to send some new fruits or other notable things they have come across to their parents and patrons. Through your kindness I, together with some other fellow countrymen, have been sent to this school chiefly for the sake of studying theology in order to be confirmed in it. My regard for you does not allow me to send you anything from here other than something concerning my studies, so that you may understand that these are a concern to me and to the others, as you commanded by your authority. Since you know, most honoured fathers, that much practice is needed if we are to attain even a measure of mediocrity in the best literature, I ought not to have opposed my teachers, who now wished me to come before the public as well. I have therefore undertaken this disputation on the amplitude of the church, which I thought fit to send to you, both so that you may see what those studies are in which our teachers here constantly exercise us, and so that I might now in some way show a grateful mind, with due reverence toward your dignity. Accept, then, most distinguished fathers, to whom I owe the greatest honour, this testimony of my study and of my affection toward you, of whatever kind it is, and henceforth keep your favour toward me and the other pupils of your piety. With God helping us, we shall take pains that the expectation you have formed of us does not disappoint you.

units.la: De amplitudine, sive multitudine & varietate credentium proximè agendum est cum adversariis, qui nobis has examinandi quæstiones dant occasionem. 1. An amplitudo sit certa veræ ac visibilis ecclesiæ nota? 2. An Romana ecclesia sit omnium amplissima. 3. An latissimè diffundi sit veræ doctrinæ Christi documentum? 4. An sola Romana doctrina sit catholica, i. e. latissimè diffusa? 5. An catholica illa orthodoxaq; doctrina & fides una cum primis istis seculis, & antę Vincentii ætatem evanuerit? 6. Si post Vincentii ætatem catholica doctrina non exspiravit, quis tandem illam professus sit præter Romanæ ecclesiæ clientes, qui mille jam & quingentos annos in orbe terrarum universo vocati sunt Christiani? 7. Quomodo orthodoxa & reformata doctrina per totum orbem dispersa sit? Examen per certas & perspicuas conclusiones, uti consuevimus, Deo vires largiente, instituemus.
units.tr: The amplitude, or multitude and variety, of believers must next be examined with our adversaries, who give us these questions to investigate. 1. Is amplitude a certain mark of the true and visible church? 2. Is the Roman church the most extensive of all? 3. Is it a proof of the true doctrine of Christ to spread most widely? 4. Is the Roman doctrine alone catholic, that is, most widely spread? 5. Did that catholic and orthodox doctrine and faith vanish along with the first ages, before the time of Vincent? 6. If catholic doctrine did not die out after the time of Vincent, who then professed it, apart from the clients of the Roman church, who for now fifteen hundred years have been called Christians throughout the whole world? 7. How has the orthodox and reformed doctrine been dispersed throughout the whole world? We shall carry out this examination by certain and clear conclusions, as we are accustomed to do, God giving us strength.

units.la: I. Conclusio prima. Amplitudo sive multitudo & varietas credentium non est certa vera ac visibilis ecclesia nota.
units.tr: I. First conclusion: amplitude, or multitude and variety of believers, is not a certain mark of the true and visible church.

units.la: Non quidem imusinfitias: ecclesiam Dei infe amplam esse, & ex orbe universo varie collectam per verbum ac Spiritum Dei, Matth. 8. v. 11. Joh. 10. 16. Psal. 2. 8. Zach. 1. v. 17. & 2. v. 10. Verumtamen sia prophanitate mundi sapienter discerni debeat, ex amplitudine judicium minime erit faciendum. Nam ipsa veritas ecclefiam non ab amplitudine commendat, non a multitudine declarat, non a magnitudine os-tendit, sed a parvitate Lucæ 12. v. 32. eam appellans τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, i.e. parvum gregem. Deinde ecclesiæ alumni dicuntur ὀλίγοι, i.e. pauci Matth. 7. v. 14. Præterea perpetuus scripturæ mos est, ut de ecclesia ad mundi comparata loquatur, tanquam de cœtu minore. Unde &c. parabolæ Christi quartam dun-taxat partem ecclesiæ vendicant, tribus aliis mundo relictis, uti Matt. 13. & Luc. 8. perspicuum est. Et omnes adoraturos esse bestiam, quorum nomina non sunt scripta in libro vitæ, scriptura testatur. Apocal. 13. 8. Horum autem familia non est angusta, non parva. Bellarmino quidem hæc nostra parum sapiunt, ideo in oppositas partes iturus, de notis ecclesiæ c. 7. quatuor objicit & quatuor alia observat, quæ qualia sint, nunc ordine videbimus.
units.tr: Indeed we do not deny that the Church of God is large, and gathered from the whole world in various ways through the Word and Spirit of God: Matt. 8. v. 11; John 10. 16; Ps. 2. 8; Zech. 1. v. 17 and 2. v. 10. Yet if it is to be wisely discerned amid the profanity of the world, judgment must by no means be made from its amplitude. For truth itself does not commend the church by its amplitude, does not declare it by its multitude, does not show it by its magnitude, but by its smallness, calling it, in Luke 12. v. 32, τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, that is, parvum gregem, "little flock." Next, the members of the church are called ὀλίγοι, that is, pauci Matth. 7. v. 14, "few." Moreover, it is the constant manner of Scripture to speak of the church as a smaller company compared with the world. Hence the parables of Christ assign to the church only a quarter, the other three parts being left to the world, as is plain from Matt. 13. & Luc. 8. And Scripture testifies that all those whose names are not written in the book of life will worship the beast, Apocal. 13. 8. The family of these is not narrow, not small. Bellarmine indeed finds our arguments of little savour, and so, going over to the opposing side, in de notis ecclesiae c. 7. he raises four objections and observes four other points; what sort these are we shall now see in order.

units.la: 2. Quantum ab objectiones, prima est.
units.tr: 2. As for the objections, the first is this.

units.la: Ecclesia verè catholica non solum debet amplecti omnia tempora, sed etiam omnia loca, omnes nationes, omnia hominum genera. Sic enim explicat quid sit esse catholicum Vin-centius Lyrinensis in suo commonitorio, ubi dicit eos proprie esse catholicos, qui tenent id, quod semper, quod ubique: quod ab omnibus credi-tum est. Resp. ¹ Etsi cum fœnore demus adveradversario, quod hîc petit, & ex Vincentio assumit: tamen nulla ratio hinc legitimè cō-ficiet, amplitudinem esse ecclesiæ notam, quæ ab aliis erroneis cætibus prudenter distingua-tur. Tanta enim amplitudo, quanta hîc pos-scitur, etiam in hæresibus nonnullis conspici-tur. Et verò ipse Mülhufinus historiarum lu-ce convictus fateri cogitur ad Arianam hære-sin olim totum orbem accessisse. de fide pag. 37. Ergone & illam, tā noxiam, tam mortiferam hæresin pro catholica ecclesia æstimabimus? 2. Deinde Vincentius viros catholicos pru-denter tanquam proprietate aliqua describit ab effectu eorum proprio, qui certè idem est cum nota, quam nos unicam unicè amplecti-mur. Qui enim credit catholicè, is omnem divinam veritatem approbat, propter divinam auctoritatem & originem. Id proprie est cre-dere, id proprie est se catholicum ostendere.
units.tr: The truly catholic church must embrace not only all times but also all places, all nations, all kinds of men. For Vincent of Lérins, in his Commonitorium, explains what it is to be catholic in this way, where he says that those are properly catholic who hold that which has been believed everywhere, always, by all. Reply: Although we grant to the adversary with interest what he seeks here and takes from Vincent, yet no sound conclusion will follow from it that amplitude is a mark of the church, which must be prudently distinguished from other erroneous assemblies. For such amplitude as is demanded here is seen even in some heresies. And indeed Mülhufinus, convicted by the light of history, is compelled to confess that the whole world once went over to the Arian heresy, On the Faith, p. 37. Shall we then also reckon that so harmful, so deadly a heresy as the catholic church? 2. Next, Vincent describes catholic men prudently by a certain property, namely their proper effect, which is certainly the same as the mark that we alone embrace. For he who believes catholically approves all divine truth, on account of divine authority and origin. That is properly to believe, that is properly to show oneself catholic.

units.la: Ex quo percipitur, Lyrinensem non papisti-cam amplitudinem, sed omnimodam veritatem ad Dei gloriam & hominum salutem utilem tanquam divinitus revelatam sive scripto, sive proloquio pro ecclesiæ nota nobiscum habere. Forma igitur catholicæ fidei non à subjectorum multitudine petatur quibus inhæret, sed ab objecti integritate ac divinitate.
units.tr: From this it is perceived that Lerinensis holds as the mark of the church not Papist amplitude, but the complete truth, useful for the glory of God and the salvation of men, as divinely revealed whether in writing or by oral tradition, just as we do. The form of catholic faith is therefore not to be sought from the multitude of the subjects in which it inheres, but from the integrity and divinity of its object.

units.la: Altera objectio est, quod prædictum est Psal. 2. Dabo tibi gentes hæreditatem tuam, & pos-sessionem sessionem tuam terminos terræ. Resp. Si syllogismus fiat, manifesta occurret fallacia consequentis. Ita enim argumentari ex hoc loco licet, Sigentes[?] sunt hæreditas Christi & termini tertæ[?] possessio ejus, amplitudo est nota ecclesiæ. Atqui verū est prius. Ergo & posteri, Nulla, nulla prorsus est ratio hujus cōsequētiæ. Id quidem confici potest, ecclesiā fore amplā, imò ampliorem, quàm ante in Judaismo. At ampliorem eam fore reliquā orbis confluge, id verò minimè hinc probatur. Nam non o-mnes gētes, sed inter gentes est ecclesia. Comparatio inibi nō est ecclesiæ cū regno Satanæ, sed cū regno & ecclesia Judaica Vet. Test., ad q; ex gētib. magna fieri accessio debuit. Tertia est ex ps. 71.8. Dominabitur à mari usq; ad mare. Resp. Hujus loci eundem esse sensum, qui prioris, certum est. Eadem igitur hinc emergit fallacia. Si enim secus accipiendus sit; absurda inde sædissima consequentur, nempe totum mundum Christo accessurum, omnes in mundo homines crediturōs, nullos super-fore ethnicos, nullos ab ecclesia alienos debere invenire. Varicinium igitur psalmæ completur, quando ex gentibus multi & æquo jure in societatem Israëliticæ ecclesiæ venerunt. Quarta est, quod Dominus Luc. ult. v. 47. & Act. 1, 8, dicit, prædicandum evangelium in omnes gentes initio facto ab Hierusalem. Resp. Syllogismus est. Si euangelium praedicandum est in omnes gentes, amplitudo est nota ecclesiae. Atqui verum est prius. Ergo & posterius. Nulla est consequentiae ratio. Rectius inde colligeres, euangelium in omnes gentes praedicandum esse ecclesiae notam, quam amplitudinem & multitudinem gentium. Non enim, ut ante dixi, fides catholica ab errore discernitur per personas, in quibus est; sed per verbum Dei, a quo est & in quod resolvitur. Haec ad obiectiones: de observationibus etiam aliquid dicamus.
units.tr: The second objection is that it has been foretold, Ps. 2: "I will give you the nations as your inheritance and possession, the ends of the earth as your possession." Reply: If a syllogism is made, a manifest fallacy of the consequent appears. For one may argue from this passage thus: the nations are Christ's inheritance and the ends of the earth his possession; amplitude is a mark of the church. But the first is true. Therefore the second. There is no reason at all for this consequence. It can indeed be concluded that the church will be large, indeed larger than before in Judaism. But that it will be larger than the rest of the crowd of the world is by no means proved from this. For the church is not all the nations, but among the nations. The comparison here is not of the church with the kingdom of Satan, but with the kingdom and church of Judaism in the Old Testament, to which a great accession from the Gentiles ought to be made. The third is from Ps. 72. 8: "He shall have dominion from sea to sea." Reply: That this passage has the same sense as the former is certain. The same fallacy therefore emerges. For if it were to be taken otherwise, most foul absurdities would follow: namely, that the whole world would come to Christ, that all men in the world would believe, that no heathen would remain, and that none should be found alien to the church. The prophecy of the psalm is therefore fulfilled when many from the Gentiles come with equal right into the fellowship of the Israelite church. The fourth is that the Lord, Luke ult. v. 47, and Acts 1. 8, says that the gospel must be preached among all nations, beginning from Jerusalem. Reply: This is a syllogism. If the gospel must be preached to all nations, amplitude is a mark of the church. But the first is true. Therefore the second. There is no reason for the consequence. More rightly you would conclude from this that the preaching of the gospel to all nations is a mark of the church, rather than the amplitude and multitude of nations. For, as I said before, catholic faith is not distinguished from error by the persons in whom it is, but by the Word of God, from which it comes and into which it is resolved. So much for the objections; let us now say something also about the observations.

units.la: Prima est ex Augusto I. de unit. eccles. c. 6. & Bedain c. 6. car. Ut ecclesia sit catholica imprimis requiri, ut non excludat ulla tempora, loca, vel hominum genera, in quo distinguitur a synagoga, quae erat ecclesia particularis, non catholica, quia erat alligata uni tempori, i. e. usque ad adventum Messiae; item uni loco i. e. templo Salomonis, extra quod non poterant sacrificare: & uni familiae, i. e. filii Jacobi. Haec observatio probata est. Attamen ecclesia fuit ante synagogam Mosaicam; & ante templum Salomonis sacrificabatur passim.
units.tr: The first is taken from Augustine, On the Unity of the Church, I, ch. 6, and from Bede, ch. 6 of the same work: for a church to be catholic, it is required above all that it exclude no times, places or kinds of men. In this it is distinguished from the synagogue, which was a particular church, not a catholic one, because it was tied to one time, that is, until the coming of the Messiah; likewise to one place, that is, the temple of Solomon, outside which they could not sacrifice; and to one family, that is, the sons of Jacob. This observation is sound. Yet the church existed before the Mosaic synagogue, and sacrifice was offered everywhere before the temple of Solomon.

units.la: Secunda est, ex Augusto, epist. 80. ad Hesychium. Ut sit ecclesia, inquit, catholica, non requiri, ut sit in omnibus hominibus totius mundi, sed tantum, ut innotescat omnibus provinciis, & in omnibus fructificet; ita ut in omnibus provinciis aliqui sint de ecclesia, donec enim enim hæc fiat, non veniet dies Domini, ut patet ex Matth. 24. Hæc observatio non modò proba est, sed & valdè utilis instituto nostro, Bellarminianis contra errorib⁹ noxia. Ita enim dubium non est, quin religio nostra sit catholica, utpote cujus fructum videamus in omnibus provinciis aut fuisse aliquem, aut adhuc esse, aut aliquando esse posse, atque etiam fore ante diem novisimum, ante cujus exortu nemo pontificius audebit nobis exprobrare religionem particularem, non catholicam, nisi hanc sit observationem parùm observan-ter habiturus. Tertia est ex Triedone lib. 4. c. 2. part. 1. de ecclesiast. dogma. Non requiri uthoc fiat simul, ut uno tempore in omnibus provinciis necessario esse oportet aliquos fideles. Satis enim est, ait, si fiat successive. Ex quo id sequitur, quòd si sola una provincia retineret veram fidem, adhuc verè & proprie dice-retur, ecclesia catholica dummodo clarè osten-deretur, eam esse unam et eandem cum illa, quæ fuit aliquo tempore, vel diversis in toto mundo. Aureis certè literis hæc observatio erat non chartis sed omnium cordibus insculpenda, qui de ecclesiæ amplitudine, quam vocant, καθολικὴν [?] lite temere admodum atque injuria nobis movent. Quarta est, quòd, etsi ecclesia non necessario debuit simul esse in omnibus locis, tamen hoc tempore debet necessario vel esse, vel fuisse in maiori parte orbis terrae. Nam ecclesia omnium consensu, etiam haereticorum, jam senuit. Si ergo in sua adolescentia & juventute non crevisset quomodo nunc in senectute crevisset? Oportet igitur ut jam creverit, atque occupaverit, si non totum orbem terrarum, at certe magnam partem. Haec nota nec vero nec praefatis assonat[?]. Quis enim Jesuitis revelavit, ecclesiam hoc tempore debere necessario velesse vel fuisse in maiori parte orbis terrarum? Absurdum & audax est effatum, sed absurdior est, atq; audacior etiam ratio, qua fulcitur. Omnium consensu, ajunt, ecclesiam jam senuisse. Quis ecclesiae, licet antiquae senium tribuat? Quis ei crementa neget & eam maturam dicat ante mesem? Ineptè etiam allegoriæ, tropi, & orationis pigmenta ad seriam rerum demonstrationem afferuntur, ex consensu logicorum. Adde, quòd observatione secunda dictum est, donec hoc fiat, diem Domini non venturum. Ergonò dies Domini jam adest ? non amplius exspectatur, sed videtur ? Fabulæ.
units.tr: The second is from Augustine, Epistle 80, to Hesychius. He says that for a church to be catholic, it is not required that it be among all the men of the whole world, but only that it be made known in all provinces and bear fruit in all of them, so that in every province there are some who belong to the church; for until this is done, the day of the Lord will not come, as is clear from Matthew 24. This observation is not only sound but also very useful to our purpose, and harmful to the errors of the Bellarmines. For there is no doubt that our religion is catholic, since we see its fruit in every province, either to have been there, or to be there still, or to be able to be there at some time, and indeed to be there before the last day; and before that day arrives, no Papist will dare to reproach us with a particular religion, not a catholic one, unless he is going to pay this observation very little heed. The third is from Triedone, Book 4, ch. 2, part 1, On the dogma of the church: it is not required that this happen at one and the same time, so that some faithful must necessarily be in all provinces at one time. For it is enough, he says, if it happens successively. From this it follows that if only one province kept the true faith, it would still be rightly and properly called the catholic church, provided it was clearly shown to be one and the same with that which existed at some time, or in various places, throughout the whole world. Surely this observation ought to be engraved with golden letters, not on paper but on the hearts of all those who rashly and most unjustly stir up the dispute over the so-called breadth of the church, the catholic [?] one, against us. The fourth is that, although the church did not necessarily have to be in all places at once, nevertheless at this time it must necessarily be, or have been, in the greater part of the world. For the church, by the agreement of all, even of the heretics, has now grown old. If, then, in its adolescence and youth it had not grown, how could it have grown now in its old age? It must therefore already have grown and occupied, if not the whole world, at least a large part of it. This point agrees neither with the truth nor with the foregoing. For who revealed to the Jesuits that at this time the church must necessarily be, or have been, in the greater part of the world? The statement is absurd and bold, but the reasoning by which it is propped up is even more absurd and bold. By the agreement of all, they say, the church has already grown old. Who would attribute old age to the church, however ancient it is? Who would deny it growth and say it is ripe before its harvest? Allegories, tropes and the ornaments of speech are also foolishly brought forward to demonstrate a serious matter, on the authority of the logicians. Add that by the second observation it was said that until this is done the day of the Lord will not come. Has, then, the day of the Lord already arrived? Is it no longer awaited but seen? Fables!

units.la: 3. Conclusio secunda. Romana ecclesia non est omnium amplissima. Ita non negamus inter caetus, qui de Christi nomine ac fide gloriantur, Romanam ecclesiam five omnem papatum hominum multitudine alios facilè æquare aut etiam superare, sed papa- tum verè credentium euangelio, ac sincerè prosiprofitentium frequentia aliis omnibus ante-cellere, id verò pernegamus. Et rectè. Nam ecclesiae magnitudo mensionem non habet ab hominibus, ut homines sunt, sed ut verae fidei confessores. Plures tales in ecclesia nostra vivere, quàm papatus habeat, non est cur ambigamus, donec ab adversariis contrarium probetur. Id exhorrent papistae, inter quos Bellarminum nunc audiemus in advetsa[?] eun-tem. Jam verò, inquit, nostram ecclesiam maximam partem orbis occupasse, & esse verè catholicam, ita probatur. Antea autem, quàm laboremus de eo, quo probetur, quod dicis, expendendum est, an certamen controversiae quod Graecis dicitur κρινόμενον[?] ita abs te attingatur. Dicis; ecclesiam vestram maximam partem orbis occupasse. Id rem acriùs intuenti, & Turcarum, aliorumq; regna recogitanti parum fit verisimile. Quanquam hîc non disputetur, an maximam orbis partem occupetis, five obsideatis, five possideatis, five teneatis, five impediatis, sed an inter vos & à vobis vera fides omnium amplissimè praedicetur, atque ideo ecclesia vestra verè catholica fit. Hoc negamus, & Bellarminus à saeculorum enumeratione hunc ferè in modum probat. Qua ecclesia tempore apostolorum in toto mundo fructificare coepit, tempore Irenaei, Tertulliani, Cypriani, Athanasii, Chrysosto-
units.tr: 3. Second conclusion. The Roman church is not the most extensive of all. We do not deny that among the assemblies which glory in the name and faith of Christ, the Roman church, or the whole Papacy, can easily equal or even surpass others in the multitude of men; but that the Papacy surpasses all others in the number of those who truly believe the gospel and sincerely profess it, that we utterly deny. And rightly so. For the greatness of the church is not measured by men as men, but as confessors of the true faith. That more such persons live in our church than in the Papacy there is no reason to doubt, until the opposite is proved by our adversaries. The Papists shrink from this, and among them we shall now hear Bellarmine, going against the adversary: Now, he says, that our church occupies the greatest part of the world and is truly catholic is proved thus. But before we labour over the proof of what you say, it must be weighed whether the matter of the controversy, which the Greeks call κρινόμενον [?], is touched upon by you in this way. You say: your church occupies the greatest part of the world. To one who looks at the matter more keenly, and considers the kingdoms of the Turks and others, this is hardly likely. Yet the question here is not whether you occupy, besiege, possess, hold or hinder the greatest part of the world, but whether the true faith is most widely preached among you and by you, and therefore whether your church is truly catholic. This we deny, and Bellarmine proves it roughly in this way, by an enumeration of the centuries: The church which began to bear fruit in the whole world in the time of the apostles, in the time of Irenaeus, Tertullian, Cyprian, Athanasius, Chrysostom,

units.la: Chrysostomi, Hieronymi, Augustini, Theodo-reti, Leonis magni, Prosperi, Gregorii, nostro denique tempore sparsa est per totum orbem, ea estamplißima & catholica. Atqui pontificia, quam Romanam dici volunt, tempore apo-stolorum in toto mundo fructificavit & tem-pore cœtero sparsa est per totum orbem. Ergo hæc est omnium amplißima & catholica. Resp. Si amplû & catholicû nostro sensu, quæ pau-lo ante expromsimus, & e sacris literis ostendi-mus capias, major admittit limitationem. Non enim est universé vera, eo quod jam tum apostolorum tempore & subsequutis etiam seculis exitiales hæreses & sectæ juxta cum ve-ra ecclesia in orbe fuerint, & quædam etiam vastissimæ, qualis erat Ariana. Quædam igi-tur ecclesia ab illo tempore diffusa est catho-lica: non omnis. Hinc autem in notescit conclusionis infirmitas. Quis enim ferat ut ex majore particulari inprima & secunda fi-gura concludatur, nisi omnis logicæ expers? Et vero nos insuper nos adjungimus ecclesiæ, quæ fructificavit tempore Pauli Col. 1. 6. Ire-næi lib. 1. c. 3. Tertulliani lib. contra Judæos c. 3. Cypriani, lib. de unitate ecclesiæ, Atha-nasii lib. de hum. verbi, Chrysostomi, Hiero-nymi & Augustini, Theodoreti, Leonis ma-gni, Prosperi, addé etiam Gregorii & nostro. Quis enim dubitaverit omni tempore, etiam
units.tr: Chrysostom, Jerome, Augustine, Theodoret, Leo the Great, Prosper, Gregory, and finally in our own time spread through the whole world, that church is the most extensive and catholic. But the Papal church, which they wish to be called Roman, bore fruit in the whole world in the time of the apostles, and in the later time has spread through the whole world. Therefore this is the most extensive and catholic. Reply: if you take "extensive and catholic" in our sense, which we have just set forth and shown from the sacred letters, the major premise admits of qualification. For it is not universally true, since already in the time of the apostles, and in the centuries that followed, pernicious heresies and sects existed alongside the true church in the world, and some very vast ones, such as the Arian. Therefore some church diffused from that time is catholic, but not every one. From this the weakness of the conclusion becomes plain. For who could bear that a conclusion should be drawn from a particular major premise in the first and second figure, unless he were quite ignorant of logic? Indeed we ourselves also join ourselves to the church which bore fruit in the time of Paul (Colossians 1:6), of Irenaeus, Book 1, ch. 3, of Tertullian, Against the Jews, ch. 3, of Cyprian, On the Unity of the Church, of Athanasius, On the Incarnation of the Word, of Chrysostom, Jerome and Augustine, of Theodoret, Leo the Great, Prosper, and to these add Gregory and our own time. For who would doubt that at every time, even

units.la: In mediis papatus tenebris ecclesiam fuisse, ac viros pios, qui à prisca apostolorum doctrina nunquam animitus & omnino discesserint? His nos accedimus lubentes, atq; ita etiam catholici jure merito dicimur. Negamus etiā, papatum esse illam ecclesiam, de qua Paulus, & allegati patres loquuntur. Multis enim ille modis à Pauli doctrina deerrat, ut alibi demonstrandi occasio erit. Sed nondum finis est gloriationum.
units.tr: in the midst of the darkness of the Papacy, there was a church, and pious men who never and utterly departed from the ancient doctrine of the apostles? We gladly join ourselves to these, and so we are rightly called catholic too. We also deny that the Papacy is that church of which Paul and the fathers cited speak. For in many ways it strays from the doctrine of Paul, as there will be occasion to demonstrate elsewhere. But the end of their boasting is not yet.

units.la: Denique nostro tempore, inquit, ecclesia Romana praeter Galliam fere totam, praeter Germaniam, Angliam, Poloniam, Boemiam, Hungariam, Graeciam, Syriam, Aethiopiam, Aegyptum, in quibus inveniuntur catholici in ipso novo orbe habet ecclesias sine admissione haereticorum, in omnibus quatuor partibus mundi; ad orientem in Indiis; ad occidentem, in America; ad septentrionem in Japonia; ad meridiem, in Brasylia, & exteriore parte Africa. At sectae haeretica nunquam totum orbem, aut certe dimidiam ejus partem occupaverunt.
units.tr: Finally, he says, in our own time the Roman church, apart from almost all of Gaul, apart from Germany, England, Poland, Bohemia, Hungary, Greece, Syria, Ethiopia, Egypt, in which Catholics are found, has churches even in the New World, without admitting heretics, in all four parts of the world: to the east in the Indies; to the west, in America; to the north in Japan; to the south, in Brazil and the outer part of Africa. But heretical sects have never occupied the whole world, or certainly not half of it.

units.la: Resp. Infinis est verbis ventosis? Aut quid exaberbat te, ut respondeas? Etiamne ego sicut vos elaquerer? Ita appositè orthodoxus cum Jobo loquatur adversariis. Quanta enim in his eorum ausis est temeritas? Orbem urbi sive papatui Romano subdunt. O vanitas! Qui probabitis, amabo vos, papismum aut totum orbe, aut dimidiam ejus partem occupasse? Sed esto, per totum orbem dispersus sit, & dispersus erit ut inter triticum zizania, & inter herbas salutares, passim lolium ac cicuta, ut in vos retorqueam, quod in ecclesiam nostram Mülhufinus pravè torserat. Hic autem non ab re notatur Bellarminiani mali loquii contradictio, qua sibi, B. Augustino, & Mülhufino contradicere non verecundatur. Una pars contradictionis est: Secta haretica nunquam totum orbem aut certè dimidiam ejus partem occupaverunt. Altera paulò post sequitur: Pulchrè Augustinus in lib. de pastor. c. 8. docet, ecclesiam esse ubique, & HÆRESIN UBIQUE. Hucpertinet illud Mülhufini p.37. Si quos habeat Italia & Hispania ejus fectatores, eos habet ut corpus benefanum, noxios, sed paucos tamen humores, & redundantia phlegmata. Germania, Gallia, Polonia, Ungaria, de quibus gloriamini, etiamsi tanto vobis numero accederet, quanto ad ARIANAM HÆRESIN OLIM TOTUS ORBIS; nihil tamen tanta accessio vestram excusaret perfidiam. Ita Cadmæi fratres mutuis se vulneribus rabidè ac furenter conficiunt, ut externis non opus sit armis, quibus societas Jesuitarum in sua viscera saevientium reprimatur ac jugulerur.
units.tr: Reply. Is there an end to windy words? Or what provokes you to answer? Should I too speak as you do? So rightly does the orthodox writer address his adversaries in the words of Job. For how great is the rashness of their claims! They subject the world to the city, or to the Roman papacy. O vanity! Who will prove, I ask you, that popery has occupied either the whole world or half of it? But grant that it is spread through the whole world. It will be spread as tares among the wheat, as darnel and hemlock among the wholesome herbs, everywhere. So I may turn back on you what Mülhufinus twisted against our Church. Here the self-contradiction of Bellarmine's wicked saying is fittingly noted, by which he is not ashamed to contradict both himself, St Augustine and Mülhufinus. One part of the contradiction is: A heretical sect has never occupied the whole world, or at least half of it. The other follows a little later: Augustine rightly teaches in his book on pastors, chapter 8, that the Church is everywhere, and HERESY EVERYWHERE. To this belongs Mülhufinus' remark on p. 37: If Italy and Spain have followers of it, they have them as a healthy body has harmful but few humours and excess phlegm. Germany, France, Poland and Hungary, of which you boast, even if they were added to you in such numbers as the whole world once was to Arian heresy, would nonetheless not excuse your perfidy. Thus the brothers of Cadmus rage and rave, destroying one another with mutual wounds, so that there is no need of outside arms by which the Society of Jesus, raging against its own vitals, may be restrained and throttled.

units.la: 4. Conclusio tertia. Latissimè diffundi non est vera doctrina Christi documentum.
units.tr: 4. Third conclusion. To be spread most widely is not a mark of the true doctrine of Christ.

units.la: Mülhufi-
units.tr: Mülhufi-

units.la: Mulhufinus quidem th. 6. p. 2. difp. de fide. Maximum etiam, ait, vera doctrina Christi documentum est, quam latissime diffundi, ficus enim catholica non fuerit. Sed vero huic ejus opinioni olim subscribere non sustinuimus, neq; jam ratio suadet melior, ut subscribamus. Non negamus, eam veræ doctrinæ indolem efle, ut nullo mundi angulo coercita in omnes gentes voce pafliva feratur. Id enim servator significat Luc. 24. & Act. 1. Id etiam sensit Vincentius Lyrinenfis cap. 3. comm.
units.tr: Mülhufinus indeed, in thesis 6, part 2, disputation on faith, says: The greatest mark of the true doctrine of Christ is that it be spread as widely as possible, for otherwise it would not be catholic. But we have never been willing to subscribe to this opinion, and no better reason now persuades us to subscribe to it. We do not deny that it is the nature of true doctrine that, confined to no corner of the world, it is carried to all nations by a passive voice. For the Saviour signifies this in Luke 24 and Acts 1, and Vincent of Lérins also perceived it in chapter 3 of his Commonitorium.

units.la: Late autem diffundi veritatis documentum atq; χεʹτιεον[?] esse, id vero pernegamus. Error enim longe lateq; diffusum est, ex mente Ciceronis de finibus, non minus quàm veritas. Ideo in locum theseos Mulhufiniæ olim substituimus hanc nostram. Apprime etiam utile est veram doctrinam indaganti, ut eam deligat, quæ tempore apostolorum in ecclesia Christi fuit latissime diffusa, i. e. catholica.
units.tr: But that to be spread widely is a mark of truth and [χεʹτιεον?], this we flatly deny. For error too has been spread far and wide, in the sense of Cicero's De finibus, no less than truth. Therefore in place of Mülhufinus' thesis we once substituted this one of ours: It is also very useful for one who seeks the true doctrine to choose that which was most widely spread in the Church of Christ in the time of the apostles, that is, the catholic.

units.la: Mens autem nostra fuit, & adhuc est, ita ostendere nullâ aliam doctrinam tutò probari posse, ceu veram, bonam ac divinam, præter eam quæ apostolorum tempore ab ecclesia Dei unanimi consensu fuit recepta creditaq:: cæteras autem opiniones, quæ à nonnullis privatim fuerint fotæ communem credendi ac vivendi regulam nulli præscribere posse aut debere. Ita ad unicam veræ religionis no-tam tetam revertimur, quam supra defendimus, verbi nempe divini communicationem; a qua una est, ut religionem veram ab aliquibus aliis, imo omnibus fictitiis tuto discernere valeamus. Rectè Chrysostomus declarat hom. 40. ad populum Antiochenum, multitudi-nem non esse notam ecclesiae. Quaenam, ait, precor, utilitas est, multum esse fœnum potius quam paucos esse lapides preciosos? Non in numeri multitudine, sed in virtutis probitate, multitudo consistit. Elias unus erat, sed totus mundus non erat dignus qui penderetur ipsi.
units.tr: Our purpose was, and still is, to show that no other doctrine can safely be proved to be true, good and divine except that which in the time of the apostles was received and believed by the Church of God with unanimous consent. Other opinions that some have held privately cannot and should not prescribe a common rule of belief and life to anyone. Thus we return to the one mark of the true religion, which we defended above, namely the communication of the divine Word. From this alone we can safely distinguish the true religion from some other religions, indeed from all fictitious ones. Chrysostom rightly declares in homily 40 to the people of Antioch that multitude is not a mark of the Church: What, I pray, is the use of there being much hay rather than a few precious stones? Multitude consists not in the number but in the uprightness of virtue. Elijah was one man, yet the whole world was not worth weighing against him.

units.la: f. Conclusio quarta. Sola Romana doctrina non est catholica, i. e. latissimè diffusa. Ita statuimus adversus Mulhusinum, qui docet solam Romanam doctrinam esse catholicam. Sensus autem conclusionis est, Romanam doctrinam, per quam hodierni papisti diu-viantes[?] errores notamus, ab ecclesia Christi non communissimè creditam, & adhuc credi: licentjam[?] à multis seculis fuerint, qui erro-ribus illis raptati, per vertiginem à primigenia veritate discesserint. Nec minus ad Augusti-num, Hieronymum, adde & Gregorium & Bernhardum, quanquam sequioribus tem-poribus vixerint, in causa religionis provo-care possumus, quàm papistæ. Confessionem enim fidei nostræ, si opus sit, ex his ipsis patribus sive cōjunctis, sive sejunctis firmare possumus. Idcirco ad summam doctrinæ, quæ ab his patribus tradita est, modò, quod fæculentum à suo quisq; sæculo traxit, aut etiam fraude citeriorum accepit, dematur, facilè calculum nostrum adjicimus. Neq; Papistæ vitio nobis vertant ac dedecori, quòd omnia isto-rum patrum scripta probare nolimus, quum nec ipsi ante probarint, varia q; prolibidine sua expurgarint, vel potius conspurcarint. Ex quo veluti principio concludimus, Mülhusi-ni Augustinum, Hieronymum, Gregorium, & Bernhardum appellantis, vaniorem esse ja-ctantiam, quàm prudentius veritatis studium.
units.tr: Fourth conclusion. The Roman doctrine alone is not catholic, that is, most widely spread. So we establish against Mülhufinus, who teaches that the Roman doctrine alone is catholic. The sense of the conclusion is that the Roman doctrine, by which we mark the errors of today's papists, has not been most commonly believed in the Church of Christ, nor is it still believed. For for many centuries there have been those who, carried off by those errors, have by giddiness departed from the primal truth. Nor can we appeal to Augustine, Jerome, and add Gregory and Bernard, though they lived in later times, in the cause of religion any less than the papists can. For we can confirm the confession of our faith, if need be, from these same Fathers, whether taken together or separately. Therefore, provided the dregs that each age has drawn in, or has received through the fraud of later times, are removed from the sum of doctrine handed down by these Fathers, we readily add our reckoning. Nor should the Papists count it a fault and a discredit to us that we are unwilling to approve all the writings of these Fathers, since they themselves did not approve them beforehand, but purged them according to their various whims, or rather defiled them. From this as a principle we conclude that Mülhufinus' appeal to Augustine, Jerome, Gregory and Bernard is more vain boasting than prudent zeal for the truth.

units.la: 6. Conclusio quinta: Catholica ortho-doxa doctrina & fides una cum primis iis fe-culis, & ante Vincentii ætatem non evanuit. Miram hic Mülhufinus φιλονεικίαν ac conten-dendi libidinem prodit, ac prurtitum. Auditè quasi hominis commentum. Miror, ait, fuferi Marpurgensis (thesi 3.) Hieronymum, caterosque veteres laudasse ecclesiam Romanam, ex hypothesi, quia in fidei puritate prae cæteris permansisse usq; ad illa tempora, quibus scripserunt; quum Vincentii ætate scripserint, illi, si ante Vincentii ætatem catholica doctrina fuerit exstincta, quod in hac thesi comminiscuntur. Argo es ecularior ac bifronte Jano qui vides etiam ea, quæ nusquam sunt. Ubi enim & quibus verbis diximus ante Vincentii ætatē cathoTo-tam hanc thesin, si[?] perlegas, ac saepius relegas, invenire ne quieris, quod per calumniam nobis objecisti. Propositum nobis fuit ostendere longe prudentius eos agere, qui religionem illam pro vera amplestuntur[?], quae apostolorum seculo & proximis ante Vincentium universe viguit, quàm quae nunc passim pluribus interpolata erroribus obtineat. Et hoc est as-ferere, religionem veram ante Vincentii aeta-tem esse exstinctam? Testes allegare volui à partium studio & aetate remotissimos, & jam omnem religionem delevi? Nempe hoc est Jesuitarum acumen, hic candor. Verba the-sis nostrae in gratiam lectoris, qui recte judica-re hanc litem voluerit, integre apponam. Apprime etiam utile est veram doctrinam indaganti, ut eam deligat, quae tempore apostolo-rum in ecclesia Christi fuit latissimè diffusa, id est, catholica. Id enim demum catholicum est, quod ubique, quod semper, quod ab omnibus creditum est, Vinc. Lyrin. comm. 3. Ea autem universalitas pro vera habenda est, quae apostolorum seculo & proximis ante Vincentium seculis in omnibus ecclesiis obtinuit. Et quidem Christi doctrinae hanc conditionem conjunctam esse ex illo Luc. ult. manifestum evadit: oportet enim in nomine ejus praedicari poenitentiam & remissionem peccatorum in omnes
units.tr: 6. Fifth conclusion: Catholic orthodox doctrine and faith, together with the first ages, and before the age of Vincent, did not vanish. Here Mülhufinus betrays a remarkable philoneikia [φιλονεικίαν], a lust for contending and an itch. Listen, as to a man's invention: "I marvel," he says, "that Fuserus of Marburg (thesis 3) has praised Jerome and the other ancients for praising the Roman church, hypothetically, because it remained in purity of faith above the others until the times in which they wrote. Since they wrote in the age of Vincent, if the catholic doctrine had been extinguished before the age of Vincent, as they invent in this thesis..." So you are more worldly-wise than two-faced Janus, who see even things that are nowhere! For where, and in what words, did we say that the catholic [doctrine was extinguished] before the age of Vincent? If you read this whole thesis through, and re-read it often, you will not find what you have falsely objected to us. Our purpose was to show that those act far more prudently who embrace as true that religion which flourished universally in the apostolic age and the immediately preceding ages before Vincent, than those who now maintain that religion, interpolated with many errors. And is this to assert that the true religion was extinguished before the age of Vincent? Did I wish to cite witnesses most remote from partisan zeal and from that age, and have I now wiped out all religion? Indeed this is the acuteness of the Jesuits, this their candour. For the sake of the reader who wishes to judge this dispute rightly, I will set out the words of our thesis in full: It is also very useful for one who seeks the true doctrine to choose that which in the time of the apostles was most widely spread in the Church of Christ, that is, the catholic. For that is at last catholic which is everywhere, always, and believed by all, Vincent of Lérins, Commonitorium 3. That universality, however, is to be held as the mark of truth which obtained in all churches in the apostolic age and in the immediately preceding ages before Vincent. And indeed that this condition is joined to the doctrine of Christ is plain from the last chapter of Luke: for repentance and remission of sins must be preached in his name to all

units.la: gentes. Ideo non tam spectandum, quæ doctrina nunc apud plures obtinet, quàm quæ olim obtinuerit, quamvis orthodoxa reformata doctrina per totum orbem dispersa fit: Italia & Hispania ( ubi decacornis bestia regnat) non paucos confessores, doctores & martyres dederit: Germania, Gallia, Polonia, Ungaria, ut hæresi infectæ sint, non exiguo tamen numero nostræ doctrinæ accedant. Britannia & Scotia solam reformatam religionem tenent: novi orbis partes, America, Brasilia &c. nostræ fidei confessores sanctissimo purpuratos martyrio, candidatos innocentiâ alunt, ut docent historiæ, negant impudenter Jesuitæ. Quis tam hebes est, ut ex his verbis contentè inspectis non intelligat, planè contrarium âme, quam adversarius calumniatur, diciac doceri? Judicet lector bonus, æquus.
units.tr: nations. Therefore we must look not so much at what doctrine now prevails among many, as at what once prevailed, although the orthodox reformed doctrine is dispersed throughout the whole world. Italy and Spain (where the ten-horned beast reigns) have given not a few confessors, teachers and martyrs. Germany, France, Poland and Hungary, though infected with heresy, nonetheless supply no small number to our doctrine. Britain and Scotland hold the reformed religion alone. The parts of the New World, America, Brazil and so on, nourish confessors of our faith, adorned with most holy martyrdom, and candidates of innocence, as the histories teach, though the Jesuits shamelessly deny it. Who is so dull that, on reading these words attentively, he does not understand that the plain opposite of what the adversary slanders is being taught? Let the good and fair reader judge.

units.la: 7. Conclusio sexta.
units.tr: 7. Seventh conclusion.

units.la: Tantum est orthodoxa doctrina confessorum, doctorum, & martyrum ab annis mille & sexcentis numerus, quantus nullis historiis, nullis verbis exprimitur. Vaniter laborat, qui eorum omnium numerum subducere conatur, qui euangelium à nato Christo professi fuêre. Multa interim nomina eorum leguntur apud Eusebium, Hieronymum, Rufinum, Socratem, Theodoretum, & antiquiores, & recentiores, qui varias eorum vices declararunt, in manibus versatur catalogus testium veritatis, crebra lectione teritur martyrologium magnum, parvum, utrumq; plenum viris veritatem professis, quorum memoria Jesuitarum impudentiam satis confundere potest. His auctoribus per lectis demū eant, & cū Mülhufino dicant: Ostendant, obsecro, tandem quis illam (veram religionem) professus sit prater ecclesiam Romanam clientes, qui mille jam & quingentos annos (priusquam cucullum exeussisset Lutherus, & seditionibus replesset Gallias Calvinus) in orbe terrarum universo, vocati sunt Christiani, eoq; nomine a Judæis, a paganis, ab hereticis, extremas injurias & persequutiones per pessi? Non illi, inquiunt, sed alii soli Deo cogniti, hominibus ignoti illam professi sunt. Frigidum hoc simul & imprudens responsum. Fateor sanè non frigidū, sed frigidissimum, non imprudens, sed & imprudentissimum esse responsum: at non ab orthodoxis datum, sed à levifido ac temerario Jesuita excogitatum, illisq; calumniosé imputatum. Sed refutationis compendium quo istorum hominum convicium dignabimur, hic à Menandro docemur:
units.tr: The number of confessors, teachers and martyrs of the orthodox doctrine from the year 1600 onward is so great that no histories and no words can express it. He labours in vain who tries to count all of those who professed the gospel from the birth of Christ onward. Meanwhile, many of their names are read in Eusebius, Jerome, Rufinus, Socrates, Theodoret, and other writers both ancient and more recent, who have described their various fortunes. The catalogue of witnesses of the truth is in people's hands, the great and small martyrologies are worn thin by frequent reading, and both are full of men who professed the truth. Their memory is enough to confound the impudence of the Jesuits. Once they have read these authors, let them go on and say with Mülhusinus: "Show me, I beg you, at last, who professed that true religion (apart from the Roman church's adherents) during the past 1,500 years, before Luther shook off his cowl and Calvin filled France with sedition, throughout the whole world, when Christians were so called, and suffered the worst injuries and persecutions from Jews, pagans and heretics on that account." "Not them," they reply, "but others, known to God alone and unknown to men, professed it." This is a cold and thoughtless answer. I admit that it is not merely cold but most cold, and not merely thoughtless but most thoughtless. Yet it was not given by orthodox men; it was devised by a flippant and rash Jesuit and falsely imputed to them. But as a brief refutation by which we may deign to answer this man's slander, we are taught here by Menander:

units.la: Ἥδιον ἴδεν, ἰδὲ μαχαιρώτερον
units.tr: Ἥδιον ἰδεῖν, ἢ μαχαιρότερον [Ἥδιον ἴδεν, ἰδὲ μαχαιρώτερον]

units.tr: Ἐς' ἡ δύνασαι λοιδορούμενον φέρειν. [Ἐς ἡ δύνασαι λοιδορούμενον φέρειν.]

units.la: Ὁ λοιδορῶν γὰρ, ἂν ὁ λοιδορούμενος
units.tr: Ὁ λοιδορῶν γὰρ, ἂν ὁ λοιδορούμενος [Ὁ λοιδορῶν γὰρ, ἂν ὁ λοιδορούμενος]

units.la: Μὴ σκευσωρήσῃ, λοιδορεῖ' ὁ λοιδορῶν, h.e.
units.tr: Μὴ σκευσωρήσῃ, λοιδορεῖ' ὁ λοιδορῶν, that is, [Μὴ σκευσωρήσῃ, λοιδορεῖ ὁ λοιδορῶν, id est]

units.la: iucundior res nulla, nec concinnior,
units.tr: nothing is more pleasant or more fitting

units.la: Conviciantem posse quàm nobis pati. Convicia etenim si tibi quis fecerit, Id dissimula: & ille ipse tum qui fecerit Tibi facta sentiet [?] sibi convicia.
units.tr: than to be able to bear with a reviler. For if anyone insults you, pass it over; and let the one who insulted you feel the insults turned back upon himself.

units.la: §. Conclusio septima.
units.tr: §. Seventh conclusion.

units.la: Orthodoxa reformataque doctrina per universum orbem vere sparsa est, ut triticum inter zizania, paleas, lolium & cicutas doctrina pontificia, cuius passim steriles dominantur avena. Hanc opponimus maledicentiae Mülhusini, qui meras zizania, lolium, cicutam, inutilia sarmenta crepat, & ineptè illud Augustini de pastoribus c. 8. in nos torquet. Non omnes haeretici, anquit, per totam faciem terrae. Alii hic, alii ibi, nusquam tamen desunt, ipsi se non noverunt. Alia Sectae in Africa, alia haeresis in oriente, alia in Aegypto, alia in Mesopotamia: diversis locis sunt diversae, sed una mater superbia omnes genuit &c. Multò sanè concinnius haec in adversariorum jugula retorquere possumus. Verùm nobis satis est labem, qua aspergimur, eluere. Doctrina nostra ut triticum per orbem seritur, quoniam nullam aliam agnoscimus, quàm Christi, quàm apostolorum, quàm à Nicenis patribus traditam, Catholica autem illa est. Ita edicunt Imperatores Gratianus, Valentinianus & Theodosius C. de summa Trinitate. Nicena fidei dudum à majoribus tradita, & divinae religionis testimonio atqz assertione firmata observantia semper mansura teneat. Is autem Nicena assertor fidei & catholicae religionis verus cultor accipiendus est: qui omnipotentem Deum & Christum filium Dei uno nomine confitetur; Deum de Deo, lumen de lumine: qui spiritum sanctum, quem ex summo rerum parente & speramus & accipimus, negando non violat: apud quem intemerata fidei sensus viget et incorrupta trinitatis individua substantia, qua graeco verbo ὁμοούσια[?] recte credentibus dicitur. Haec profecto nobis magis probanda, hac veneranda sunt. Desi-nant igitur vitilitigatores doctrinā reforma-tæ ecclesiæ sugillare, & discant cum piis impe-ratoribus & ecclesia nostra solo Dei ver-bo niti, quod unum est veritatis magisterium, omnis erro-ris, vanitatis, hæresis in capax.
units.tr: Orthodox and reformed doctrine has truly been sown throughout the whole world, like wheat among tares, chaff, darnel and hemlock, which is the papal doctrine, and over which barren oats rule everywhere. We set this against the slander of Mülhusinus, who cries out that there are nothing but tares, darnel, hemlock and useless branches, and who clumsily turns against us that saying of Augustine about shepherds, chapter 8: "Not all heretics," he says, "are throughout the whole face of the earth. Some are here, others there, yet they are never wholly absent, though they do not know one another. One sect is in Africa, another heresy is in the East, another in Egypt, another in Mesopotamia. They are different in different places, yet pride, one mother, gave birth to them all," and so on. We could certainly turn these words back upon our adversaries's throats much more neatly. But for us it is enough to wash off the stain with which we are smeared. Our doctrine is sown through the world like wheat, since we acknowledge no other than the doctrine of Christ, of the apostles, and of that handed down by the Nicene fathers; and that is the catholic doctrine. So the emperors Gratian, Valentinian and Theodosius decreed in the Code, concerning the highest Trinity: "The faith of Nicaea, handed down long ago by our ancestors and confirmed by the testimony and assertion of divine religion, shall remain ever in force and be kept." The Nicene defender of the faith and true worshipper of the catholic religion is to be accepted as one who confesses almighty God and Christ the Son of God under one name; God from God, light from light; who does not violate the Holy Spirit, whom we hope for and receive from the highest parent of all things, by denying him; in whom the undamaged sense of the faith flourishes, and the undivided substance of the incorrupt Trinity, which by the Greek word is rightly said by believers to be consubstantial [ὁμοούσιον]. Surely these are what we should rather approve, these are what we should revere. Let the idle wranglers therefore cease to disparage the doctrine of the reformed church, and let them learn, with the pious emperors, that our church rests on the word of God alone, which is the one teaching authority of truth, and admits no error, vanity or heresy.

units.la: AD ORNATISSIMUM JUVENEM D. JOHANNEM IRENÆUM, SS. THEOL. STUDIOSUM PULPITA PUBLICA CONSCENSURUM, AMICUM AC FRATREM CHARISSIMUM.
units.tr: TO THE MOST DISTINGUISHED YOUNG MAN, MR. JOHANN IRENAEUS, STUDENT OF SACRED THEOLOGY, ABOUT TO MOUNT THE PUBLIC PULPITS, MY FRIEND AND MOST DEAR BROTHER.

units.la: Est dubium multis ecclesia quæ sit in orbe, Dum turbant populum dogmata pontificum. Idcirco multi misere sub mole laborant In tenebrisq; errant perdita sicut ovis.
units.tr: Many are unsure which church is in the world, while the dogmas of the pontiffs trouble the people. Therefore many labour wretchedly under the burden, and wander in darkness, lost like sheep.

units.la: Interea clarum, claro de lumine lumen Per verbum Domini Christus in orbe micat. Verba docent ejus, sit quænam ecclesia vera Demonstrans populo dulce salutis iter.
units.tr: Meanwhile it is clear: light from light, Christ shines in the world through the Word of the Lord. His words teach which church is the true one, showing the people the sweet road of salvation.

units.la: Hanc qui studet clare doctrinam reddere Doctor Ingenio Crocius, judicioq; gravis: Dum verbo Domini, tot cæca sophismata solvit Ac Christi cœrus [?] vera sigilla notat.
units.tr: Doctor Crocius, a man of keen mind and grave judgement, who strives to make this doctrine plain: while by the Word of the Lord he dissolves so many blind sophisms, and marks the true seals of the assembly of Christ.

units.la: Hanc ut defendas tua te, Irenæ fidelis, Admonet hoc pietas officiumq; tuum. Et præeunte tibi docto Doctore, sophistas Ut vincas, mandat religionis amor.
units.tr: That you may defend it, faithful Irenaeus, your own piety and duty admonish you. And with the learned Doctor going before you, the love of religion commands you to conquer the sophists.

units.la: Ergo tibi frater, Christus dignetur adesse [?] Pugnantiq; suam porrigat ipse manum. Tu vero confide Deo, Deus optimus ille Et studia & vitæ diriget ipse tuas.
units.tr: Therefore, brother, may Christ deign to be present with you, and may he himself stretch out his hand to you in the fight. But trust in God: that most good God himself will direct your studies and your life.

units.la: Ut possis prodesse bonis, servireq; Christo Et post hanc vitam regna tenere poli.
units.tr: So that you may be able to benefit good people and serve Christ, and after this life possess the kingdoms of heaven.

units.la: Adamus Hartmannus, Bohemus
units.tr: Adam Hartmann, Bohemian
